facts.fact: Sao Tome and Principe's Cadastro Social Unico, set up by Decreto-Lei 16/2018 and regulated by Decreto-Lei 3/2023, was expanded by a data update from 8,000 to more than 12,500 households, the prime minister said (RSTP).
The Direcao da Protecao Social says about 12,500 households, 25% of the population, are registered in the Cadastro Social Unico, a system built to identify and target support to vulnerable families.

systems.owner: Direcao da Protecao Social, Solidariedade e Familia

facts.fact: The DPSSF reports it updated 12,560 households and 52,808 individuals in the Cadastro Social Unico in a 2026 recertification and expansion from 8,000 to 12,000 households.

systems.owner: Direcção da Proteção Social, Solidariedade e Família

note: No fact on use by two or more programmes or on a national ID link; only the Programa Família Vulnerável is named as drawing on it.

facts.fact: The Labour Minister said on 27 January 2026 that the Cadastro Social Único system already works and is being improved from eight thousand to twelve thousand households.

systems.owner: Direção de Proteção Social, Solidariedade e Família

facts.fact: The World Bank project paper says São Tomé and Príncipe's Unique Social Registry was launched in 2024 and holds data on 8,740 families, about 16% of the national population.

systems.owner: Government of São Tomé and Príncipe (Ministry of Labor, Solidarity, and Social Security)

note: Social protection is only listed as a service area and a Phase 3 sector; no social registry is named.
Document is about the electoral roll; it states nothing on a social registry.

facts.fact: openIMIS says Ke-Non holds a Unique Social Registry database, whose data for more than 10,000 families eligible for the cash transfer were updated between December 2023 and February 2024.

RSTP reports that the fourth Programa Família Vulnerável payment to 6,000 families is the first after the recertification and expansion of the Cadastro Social Único, per DPSSF director Núria de Ceita.

The DPSSF press note describes the Cadastro Social Único as the country's largest social protection database, being recertified and expanded, with a pilot survey on digital tools from 17 to 20 February 2026 in three districts.
The DPSSF says the Cadastro Social Único is the reference instrument for several programmes, among them Programa Família Vulnerável and the Apoio à Criação do Próprio Emprego component.

systems.owner: DPSSF, Ministry of Labour, Solidarity and Social Security

facts.fact: RSTP, citing a DPSSF communique, describes the Cadastro Social Único as an information system and database run by the DPSSF to classify households, with Programa Família Vulnerável households required to update their data by 10 April 2026.
